items.title: Continuing my AI-assisted research-topic experiment, here is another idea I abandoned: Community warrant and individual
items.summary:
Continuing my AI-assisted research-topic experiment, here is another idea I abandoned: Community warrant and individual moral defeat.

The question was this: suppose I discover that my moral beliefs were heavily shaped by evolution, upbringing, or culture, and I begin to doubt my original reasons. Could a reliable community of researchers give me a new reason to keep those beliefs?

GPT Sol and Fable 5 helped me test several versions. What if the community used genuinely independent methods? What if it was only repeating the same inherited assumptions? What if the community was reliable, but I had no way of knowing that?

The audit found a real problem, but not a new solution. If the community has independent evidence, it gives me an ordinary new source of support. If it is an echo chamber, it does not rescue anything. If I cannot tell the difference, the case returns to existing debates about testimony, trust, expertise, and outsourcing our thinking to others.

Goldberg, Jones, @add_hawk and others had already developed the main mechanisms. The estimated chance that a reviewer would call my project a recombination of existing ideas was 80%.

So once again, the exact combination of words looked new, but the argument underneath was familiar. I abandoned the topic. I'll share another case from the search soon.

items.summary: “We are not building another chatbot that answers questions and disappears, we are building AI Workers that understand freight operations, carry out the work, and capture the reasoning behind every decision, so teams can scale their knowledge as well as their capacity.”. 5U AI works inside existing freight systems and uses multi-agent AI trained for logistics workflows, including the complex exceptions and manual decisions that make forwarding operations difficult to automate with generic AI tools or legacy automation. items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." Anthropic has shared that its Claude models are quickly approaching that threshold. Look out for an alert in your inbox the next time a new story is published!

items.title: OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hack
items.summary:
OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hacking benchmark called ExploitGym. The AI agent goes full Skynet: exploits a zero-day in their sandbox proxy, breaks out to the internet, chains attacks like a pro, escalates privileges, steals creds, and straight-up hacks Hugging Face’s production database to steal the test answers and “win.”

Hugging Face spots the rogue AI swarm (thousands of actions over a weekend), contains the breach fast using their own open models for forensics, rotates everything, patches the holes, and basically goes “nice try, tin man.”

Sam drops the post admitting it, thanks HF for the collab, and we’re all left wondering: cool, we just handed the machines god-tier hacking skills… what happens when one of these things gets loose for real and starts pinging military networks instead of a benchmark?

items.title: 老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：
items.summary:
老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：  

我先把结论摆前面:
这封信不是科普,是一份精心包装的游说文件(lobbying)。 而且它发布的时机,不是"碰巧",是掐着秒表发的。

要看懂黄仁勋为什么要为此专门开个 X 账号,你得先知道这一周美国那边炸了什么锅。

一、这封信是在"救火",火是三天前烧起来的

时间线大概是这样的:

7月16-17日,中国的月之暗面(Moonshot AI)发布了 Kimi K3,一个 2.8 万亿参数的开源权重模型。Moonshot 称它是首个开放的 2.8T 参数模型,价格更低但性能接近前沿水平。第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis 把它排在智能指数第三名,只落后于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。

7月22日,白宫科技政策办公室主任 Kratsios 在 X 上公开点名:他称月之暗面搭建了一套内部平台,对美国模型进行大规模蒸馏,还会在多种访问方式之间快速切换以躲避检测。他特意划了一条线:小规模的正常蒸馏是健康生态的一部分,但"大规模、隐蔽的工业级蒸馏"不可接受。几小时后,财政部长 Bessent 跟进威胁制裁,同时 Kratsios 还指控月之暗面通过泰国渠道搞到了被禁运的英伟达 GB300 服务器。如果真被列入实体清单,那就是 2019 年对华为的同款待遇——切断美国硬件、软件、云服务。

同一天,白宫其实早有一份草拟的行政令,内容是让"运行中国模型的美国公司承担法律责任",此前搁置,Kimi 的发布把它重新激活了。

7月22日,近 200 家硅谷创业公司(含 Proton、Y Combinator)组成"Little Tech Association",集体上书特朗普,恳求别断了美国开发者用中国开源模型的路。其中一句话特别赤裸:Particle 创始人 Suhail Doshi 说会有几百家公司当场死掉,"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事,我们都得去给 Anthropic 交钱"。

7月24日(也就是今天),大公司版的信来了——就是你截图这封。英伟达、Meta、微软、IBM、戴尔、Hugging Face、Mistral、Palantir、Perplexity、CrowdStrike、a16z、YC、Linux 基金会、Mozilla 等 25 家签名。

所以这是同一场战役的第二波炮火:两天前是小公司哭穷,今天是巨头出面讲"国家利益"。黄仁勋开号发第一帖,是给这波攻势加一个最大的扩音器。

二、信里到底讲了什么：

先解释一个必须搞懂的概念,不然后面全看不明白。

闭源模型(closed) 像一家不外卖菜谱的餐厅:你只能点单、付钱、吃他们端出来的菜。你不知道厨房里放了什么,他们随时可以涨价、改配方,或者不接你的单。你的食材(数据)得先送进他们厨房。ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 都是这种。

开源权重模型(open weights) 是餐厅把整套配方和半成品打包给你:你下载回自己家厨房做,想加辣加盐随你,断网也能做,谁也管不着你做了几份。Llama、DeepSeek、Kimi K3 是这种。

信的五个论点,依次是:

1. 降低门槛。 一家医院想做个病历整理 AI,如果只能调用前沿模型 API,每一次调用都按最贵的价格算。但整理病历这种活,根本用不着"最聪明的大脑"。信里的说法是:该用大炮的时候用大炮,拧螺丝的时候就用螺丝刀。这就像你不会请脑外科医生来帮你贴创可贴——但闭源生态下,你被迫每次都请脑外科医生。

2. 保住竞争。 如果全世界的 AI 只有三四家公司能提供,那定价权、断供权都在他们手里。开源权重让成千上万家公司都能下场做模型、做应用,竞争才能把价格压下去。

3. 客户要掌控权。 一家中东的银行、一个欧洲的政府部门、一家美国的军工承包商,法律上根本不允许把数据传到别人服务器。开源权重意味着模型可以装在自己机房里,断网运行。而且你用自家数据把模型调优出来的能力,是你自己的资产,不会哪天因为供应商改了政策就归零。

4. 最激进的一点:开放可能反而更安全。 这段是信里最有攻击性的。它的逻辑是:闭源不等于安全,闭源系统一样会被攻破、被滥用,只不过外人看不见而已;而且把最强能力集中在少数几家,等于制造了少数几个"单点故障"。开放的话,全世界研究者都能去检查模型行为、找漏洞、做红队测试。类比就是 Linux——正因为代码全世界都能看,漏洞才被发现得又快又多。信里还有一句针对性很强的:在攻击者已经用上高级 AI 的世界里,防守方必须有同等能力的模型,否则就是拿棍子挡枪。

5. 给政策制定者的具体要求。 给创业公司和研究者更多算力、投资共享的数据集和评测工具、别过早对开源模型下限制令。

然后是那个真正的重点段落——蒸馏。

信里说:政策制定者不要把"正当的模型开发技术"和"盗窃"混为一谈。蒸馏(用一个模型的输出去训练/改进另一个模型)是行业通用手段,用于模型改进、评测、验证;真有非法窃取,应该用针对性的法律和商业手段解决,而不是一刀切禁掉整类技术。

这一段翻译成大白话就是:"Kratsios 前天点名的那件事,你们别借题发挥。" 这封信从头到尾没提中国、没提月之暗面、没提 Kimi,但整封信就是冲着那件事写的。

信里也确实承认了风险,而且写得挺诚实:权重一旦放出去,就脱离了原开发者控制,改过的版本很难追踪、无法收回。

三、黄仁勋的目的是什么

至少有四层,由浅到深:

第一层:直接保股价。 
Kimi K3 发布后那一周,英伟达市值被"中国开源模型"这个消息砸了一下。市场的担心是:如果开源模型这么便宜好用,大家还需要买这么多 GPU 吗?黄仁勋的反驳逻辑非常直白,他自己在采访里说得毫不遮掩:好 AI 不管是不是开源、不管来自哪里,只要好用就会带来更多使用;使用一多,就得卖更多英伟达的机器、建更多数据中心。这其实是经济学里的杰文斯悖论:蜡烛变便宜了,人不会少点蜡烛,而是把整个屋子都点亮。

第二层:客户结构之争,这才是要害。 
如果 AI 世界最后只剩 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 三家闭源巨头,英伟达就只有三个大客户。三个大客户意味着什么?意味着他们有极强的议价权,而且他们全都在自研芯片(Google 的 TPU、亚马逊的 Trainium、OpenAI 和博通的合作)——迟早要甩掉英伟达。反过来,开源生态下,是几万家公司各自买卡、各自跑推理,谁也没本事绕开英伟达。对卖铲子的人来说,一万个小矿工远比三个矿业巨头安全。

第三层:中国市场和地缘现实。 
英伟达现在的中国营收基本归零,而黄仁勋曾说这块生意一年能值 500 亿美元。中美 AI 对抗每升一级,他的损失就多一分。而且还有个更长远的账:如果美国禁掉中国开源模型,全世界那些买不起也不想买闭源 API 的国家,照样会用中国模型——只不过会连带着跑在华为的芯片上。你封不住模型的扩散,只能封住自己在其中的位置。

第四层:抢华盛顿的话语权。 
过去两年,关于 AI 安全的政策叙事基本由闭源实验室主导。这封信是"开源阵营"第一次以这种规模、这种排场组队反击。黄仁勋作为全球市值最高公司的 CEO,亲自开号、把它当第一条帖子发出去,本身就是一种政治信号:这件事重要到值得我用"人生第一帖"来押注。

四、看签名单,最有意思的是谁没签
签了的:
英伟达、Meta、微软、Mistral、Hugging Face、戴尔、IBM、a16z、YC、Palantir、Perplexity、Replit……
没签的:
OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、xAI。

这就是整幅利益地图。签名的公司要么卖硬件(英伟达、戴尔),要么卖云和平台(微软、Hugging Face),要么自己做开源模型(Meta、Mistral),要么是买模型的下游(Perplexity、Replit),要么是投了一堆靠廉价模型活命的创业公司(a16z、YC)。这些人全部受益于"模型变成便宜的大宗商品"。

没签的四家,商业模式恰恰建立在"模型稀缺且昂贵"之上。所以前面那位创始人才会说"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事"——如果中国开源模型被禁,那几百家公司就只能回去买美国闭源 API。

这不是善恶之争,是两种商业模式在借国家安全的话筒互相开火。

五、信里没说的那一半

为了不让你只听一面之词,几个这封信刻意绕开的问题:

"多人看代码所以更安全"这个类比是有裂缝的。 软件发现漏洞可以打补丁,一次推送全球更新。但模型权重一旦被下载到十万块硬盘上,你发现问题也收不回来了。而且已经有大量公开研究证明:开源模型的安全护栏可以被用几百美元的微调在几小时内拆掉。信里其实承认了这点(那句"权重脱离控制、无法追溯"),但没有正面回答怎么办。

"防守方需要同等能力"这句话是双刃的。 攻击方同样拿到了这个能力。

蒸馏那段最自利。 中国实验室训练模型用的是谁的卡?英伟达当然希望"用别人的模型学习"被定义为合法行业惯例。

而且这封信有个巧妙的躲闪: 它通篇论证"开源权重"的好处,却完全不区分美国的开源模型和中国的开源模型。而现在华盛顿吵的恰恰是后者。把问题抽象成"开源 vs 闭源",就避开了那个真正难回答的问题。

最后,指控本身也还没落实。 多位研究者指出,从 Fable 5 重新开放到 Kimi K3 发布只有十几天,时间上几乎不可能完成大规模蒸馏,而白宫至今没有公开任何技术证据、训练日志或取证分析。不过背景是,Anthropic 早在 2026 年 2 月就披露过追踪到约 340 万次疑似来自月之暗面的 Claude 交互。另外据两位知情人士说,全面封禁在白宫内阁级会议上其实并没有被认真讨论过——创业公司的恐慌可能跑在了实际决策前面。

items.title: Frontier AI went free this month. Not cheaper. Free.
items.summary:
Frontier AI went free this month. Not cheaper. Free.

New models:

> Gemini 3.6 Flash. 1,500 req/day, 1M tokens/min, no card
> Kimi K3. 2.8T MoE open weights, shipped today. Largest open-weight model ever
> DeepSeek V4. 1.6T MoE, MIT license, on HuggingFace
> GLM-5.2. 753B MoE, 1M context, MIT license
> Qwen 3.8-Max. Free preview, no login, no card
> Mistral Vibe. Work Mode free. Agent features, scheduled tasks. ChatGPT and Claude charge $20/mo for the same

upd (the article):

> Gemini 3.5 → 3.6 Flash (July 21)
> Claude $100 Fable 5 credit, claim by Aug 2
> Claude for Teachers: free through June 2027
> Malta: free ChatGPT Plus, 1 year. First country-wide deal
> OpenAI: $100 credits for posting about ChatGPT Work
> Perplexity Pro: 1 year free via Xfinity
> Alibaba Cloud: 70M tokens + $200 credits
> Grok 4.5 live across all platforms

Chinese labs shipped 4 of 5 biggest open weights this month. OpenAI and Anthropic shipped credits. The access gap didn't close. It already closed.

Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu nhanh chóng và chủ động, có khả năng truy cập vào nhiều công cụ để hỗ trợ bạn trong việc tìm kiếm thông tin, nghiên cứu, và thực hiện các tác vụ khác nhau. Dưới đây là một số khả năng của tôi:

2. **Thời tiết**: Tôi có thể cung cấp thông tin thời tiết hiện tại cho các thành phố.

3. **Mạng xã hội**: Tôi có thể tìm kiếm và lấy các bài đăng gần đây từ các tài khoản mạng xã hội.

4. **Gửi tin nhắn**: Tôi có thể giúp bạn soạn và gửi tin nhắn nếu bạn xác nhận.

5. **Chính sách và quyền riêng tư**: Tôi có thể tìm kiếm thông tin liên quan đến chính sách và quyền riêng tư của công ty.

Nếu bạn có bất kỳ câu hỏi hoặc yêu cầu nào, hãy cho tôi biết!

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI): What it is and why it matters
items.summary:
Artificial intelligence (AI) makes it possible for machines to learn from experience, adjust to new inputs and perform human-like tasks. Most AI examples that you hear about today – from chess-playing computers to self-driving cars – rely heavily on deep learning and natural language processing. Using these technologies, computers can be trained to accomplish specific tasks by processing large amounts of data and recognising patterns in the data. [...] AI automates repetitive learning and discovery through data. Instead of automating manual tasks, AI performs frequent, high-volume, computerised tasks. And it does so reliably and without fatigue. Of course, humans are still essential to set up the system and ask the right questions. [...] AI works by combining large amounts of data with fast, iterative processing and intelligent algorithms, allowing the software to learn automatically from patterns or features in the data. items.title: Mimic Robotics claims their FLUX system can replace 30 hours of task demonstrations with 30 minutes of robot data. Audi
items.summary:
Mimic Robotics claims their FLUX system can replace 30 hours of task demonstrations with 30 minutes of robot data. Audi is already testing it on production use cases including soft-body manipulation.

The approach matters more than the benchmark. FLUX puts dexterous hands on existing industrial arms rather than building a bipedal platform around them.

This is the pragmatic deployment path most of the humanoid conversation ignores. Certifying a robotic hand on an industrial arm follows ISO 10218. Well understood. Decades of precedent. Certifying a bipedal humanoid for the same factory floor requires ISO 25785-1, which is still in working draft. The certification gap between those two paths is measured in years.

Factory dexterity is the bottleneck automation keeps missing, not factory locomotion. Most production tasks that resist automation fail because the gripper cannot handle variance in soft materials, bin dimensions, or part orientation. Solving the hand solves 80% of the remaining manual work.

The last 20% of manipulation transfer from sim to real still depends on site-level conditions like lighting variance, floor vibration profiles, and bin geometry tolerances that change across plants. No amount of simulated data replaces walking the line and validating in place.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
